text:
marie.k: Quick proposal — I'd like to split the onboard pipeline into two orthogonal stages: a super-fast 'smoke' path for runtime compatibility and artifact sanity, and a slower 'bench' path for throughput/quality profiling. Reason: teams keep waiting for full bench runs when the runtime-level checks would have caught blockers earlier.

sanjay: +1. Do you mean separate CI jobs or different internal services?

marie.k: Separate jobs but with defined contracts. Smoke runs inline on ingest (goal: < 5m), checks: model load, KV cache sanity, tokenization mismatch, basic forward pass on a tiny batch, signature/hash check. Bench runs async (hours) and produce perf/quality artifacts.

oliver: How do we ensure bench results are linked back to the artifact used by smoke? Need reproducible IDs.

marie.k: We'll stamp the model artifact with an immutable manifest: model_id, commit_hash, quantization_profile, build_kernels_version, container_image. Smoke gates on manifest + short runtime probes. Bench consumes same manifest and writes results to model registry entry.

anya: What about version compatibility with runtime kernels? Example: a model converted with newer attention kernel might pass smoke but fail at scale.

marie.k: Good call. Smoke should include a quick kernel-exercise: run 1-2 steps with the runtime path we plan to serve on (including quantized path if present). Not full perf but checks ln(kernel) paths.

sanjay: Tradeoffs: if smoke includes kernel probing, it becomes heavier. We should be strict about what "kernel exercise" means. Maybe limit to seq len 64 and 1-2 batch.

oliver: Agreed. Also need an interface boundary: smoke should only require runtime client api (e.g., start_session, forward_step) not internal runtime internals. That keeps it portable across private/dedicated.

marie.k: Exactly. Proposed minimal smoke API: { start_session(manifest), run_inputs(list[str]), check_kv_cache(), fetch_metrics() } — opaque responses but deterministic pass/fail.

anya: Can we gate deployment based on smoke + cached bench baseline? Example: allow canary if smoke passes and bench baseline exists (not necessarily fresh).

marie.k: Yes — fallback policy: if no fresh bench, allow canary with stricter traffic weight and realtime perf monitoring. If smoke fails, reject immediately.

sanjay: How do we record failures for quicker debugging? Need structured logs and a short failure code set.

marie.k: Use small triage schema: FAILURE:LOAD, FAILURE:KERNEL_MISMATCH, FAILURE:TOK_MISMATCH, FAILURE:INF_NAN, FAILURE:SIGNATURE. Smoke outputs one code and minimal logs (first 100 lines).

oliver: For bench: we should produce artifacts that drive Optimize recommendations — throughput, p95 latency, cost-per-token, and quality eval on a small eval set. Bench should version the eval set used.

anya: Also add a quick checksum of quantized weights to detect accidental re-quantizations.

marie.k: Will do. I sketched a gate config YAML for the pipeline:```yaml
pipeline:
  smoke:
    timeout: 300  # seconds
    checks:
      - load
      - tokenization
      - kernel_probe:
          seq_len: 64
          batch: 2
  bench:
    async: true
    resources: gpu-large
    eval_set: release/smoke_eval_v2
    metrics:
      - throughput
      - p95
      - quality: rouge
fallbacks:
  allow_canary_if_no_bench: true
  canary_traffic_limit: 0.05
```

sanjay: Nice. A couple of operational notes: 1) Smoke must be cheap — aim for <= $0.20 per run. 2) Bench scheduling should be quota-aware. 3) Provide a manual override for SRE/product when rapid rollout is needed.

marie.k: Agreed. For (1) we'll run smoke on tiny CPU/GPU nodes depending on artifact. For (2) bench will enqueue into reserved bench pools with prioritization. For (3) manual override requires two approvals and auto-rollback if smoke/metrics trip after deploy.

oliver: Interface boundary proposal: the ingest service emits manifest + signed checksum. A runtime-adapter service implements the smoke client against the target runtime. That adapter returns pass/fail + code. Registry stores both manifest and smoke verdict.

anya: How do we handle private deployments (on-prem)? Customer may not want bench data uploaded. Bench can be optional and only store minimal meta back to registry. Smoke needs to run in customer infra or via agent.

marie.k: For private: run smoke agent in customer VPC that reports only pass/fail + code and manifest hash. Bench optional and can remain on-prem; we only store pointer if customer allows. Documented in private-deploy playbook.

deploy-bot: Notice: created ticket ML-4676 for "split smoke/bench pipeline + manifest contract" (link: https://boards.internal/ML-4676).

sanjay: Action items: (1) marie to draft RFC with schema for manifest + triage codes, (2) oliver to prototype runtime-adapter client, (3) anya to write private-deploy playbook section.

marie.k: I'll have the RFC draft by EOD Friday and wire up a minimal smoke runner prototype next week. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
